questions.q: What makes Dana Whitfield's combination of Claims Adjuster and Payment Approver a toxic combination specifically?
options: Held together, they let one person originate a claim payment request and approve its own disbursement, with no second set of eyes at any point
Claims Adjuster and Payment Approver are the same role under two different names
The combination is only risky if the account also has administrator access to the network
Both roles are individually too broad and should never be assigned to anyone
questions.explain: A toxic combination is two individually reasonable permissions — originate and approve — that become dangerous only when one account holds both.

questions.q: Why did this combination go undetected for fourteen months?
options: The combination only became risky after the merger with Castellan
Dana actively hid the combination from her managers
Access certification campaigns had already caught and cleared it twice before
Thornbury's RBAC role catalog never encoded a mutual-exclusion rule between the two roles, and no separation-of-duties check ever ran to flag the pairing
questions.explain: The gap was in the role catalog and the lack of an SoD check, not anything Dana did — it existed because no control was designed to catch it.

questions.q: What did the investigation find when it cross-referenced roughly 230 claims Dana originated against who approved each one?
options: The records had been deleted and could not be reviewed
Half of her claims were self-approved
Zero instances where she approved her own claim — the exposure was real, but no fraud actually occurred
She had approved every claim she originated herself
questions.explain: The investigation sized the risk accurately: a real gap and real exposure existed, but the review found no actual self-approved transactions.

questions.q: What is the immediate remediation step taken on Dana's account?
options: No immediate action is taken until the full investigation concludes
The Payment Approver role is revoked while she keeps Claims Adjuster, and an uninvolved backup approver is assigned
Both roles are revoked and her account is suspended pending termination
She is given additional roles to balance out the conflict
questions.explain: The quick fix removes only the conflicting role she doesn't need for her actual job, while keeping her able to do her real work.

questions.q: What is the structural, preventive fix put in place so this type of gap doesn't recur with a different pair of roles?
options: A separation-of-duties check written as code, run nightly against the role-assignment table, plus a mutual-exclusion rule added to the formal role catalog
A memo asking managers to check for toxic combinations manually once a year
Removing all approval roles from the organization entirely
Requiring every employee to hold only one role for the rest of their tenure
questions.explain: The controls-as-code SoD check and the catalog-level mutual-exclusion rule both prevent the combination from being granted or from going unnoticed again.
